issue.title: memory-directory-map.png and its prompt still label memory tiers short/long after the core/reference rename
issue.description: The packaged memory-architecture infographic and the prompt that generates it still describe memory tiers with the retired short/long vocabulary.

task_type_fields.impact:
Epic sase-sq phase sase-sq.1 (commit c9ca0db5f) renamed the memory tiers to core/reference everywhere else: frontmatter is `type: core` / `type: reference`, the AGENTS.md anchors are `## Tier 1 (core) Memory` / `## Tier 2 (reference) Memory`, and every doc and skill was swept. This packaged infographic is the last surface still teaching `short`/`long` as the current spelling rather than as an accepted legacy alias, so a reader of the shipped memory diagram learns retired vocabulary.

Proposed by phase bead sase-sq.1 (note 4) and routed here by the sase-sq land agent. The prompt file and the PNG must be regenerated together so the labels do not drift apart: fix the four label lines, re-render `memory-directory-map.png` from the updated prompt with an image model, and commit both. Regenerating the PNG needs image-generation capability that a code agent does not have, which is why the land agent could not discharge this as epic work.
task_type_fields.repro: Run `grep -n "short\|long" src/sase/memory/assets/memory-directory-map.prompt.md`. Four lines still describe the retired vocabulary: line 19 ("canonical short and long notes"), line 54 (``type: short | long``), and lines 55-56 ("Tier 1 short notes", "Tier 2 long notes"). The rendered `memory-directory-map.png` beside it carries the same labels; `git log -1 -- src/sase/memory/assets/memory-directory-map.prompt.md` shows 86c9b3181, a prose-width change that predates the rename, so neither file was touched by epic sase-sq.
